MSA redline expectations and DPA data residency
SLA tiers and billing path for committed capacity

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-23
Time: 15:00 - 15:58 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Sam Patel (Redwood AE), Lena Cho (Redwood SE), Diego Ramos (Redwood CSM), Marcus Lee (HelioPay Procurement), Aisha Khan (HelioPay Legal), Ravi Menon (HelioPay FinOps), Tara O'Neill (HelioPay Security)

---
00:00 Sam: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Sam here from Redwood, I'm the AE on this account. Quick roll call?
00:12 Marcus: Marcus here.
00:14 Aisha: Aisha on legal.
00:16 Ravi: Ravi, FinOps.
00:18 Tara: Tara, security.
00:20 Sam: Great. Lena and Diego from our side, quick introductions...
00:28 Lena: Hi all, I'm Lena, solutions engineer, will cover SOC2/KMS and dedicated deployment questions.
00:33 Diego: Diego, customer success, I'll help with onboarding and billing flows.
00:38 Marcus: Cool, main agenda for us: we need to understand pricing bands, commit vs overage, MSA/DPA timing, and what you need from procurement to move the approval along.
00:47 Sam: Perfect, we'll walk through the pricing spreadsheet first then discuss legal artifacts.

03:12 Sam: So, the offer we put on the table is three commitment bands — small, mid, and enterprise — each with a committed monthly token/embedding unit. The higher the band the better per-unit rate and a shorter invoice cadence is negotiable.
03:36 Ravi: Can you say more about true-up and overage? If we commit and don't use it, how does that reconcile?
03:44 Lena: Yeah so there's a monthly true-up model. If you underuse the commit, typically there's no refund but we can structure credits or carry-forward in some cases — that's negotiable on enterprise deals. If you overuse, overage rates apply; we can also cap overage in the SOW for predictability.
04:05 Ravi: Hmm, credits help but we need clarity for FinOps forecasting. Can you show an example?
04:11 Sam: Sure, I'll share the spreadsheet after the call. Example: mid band commit 500M tokens/month at $X/token, overage at 1.5x the committed rate, but if you commit annually we can reduce overage multiplier to 1.2x.

06:30 Marcus: How does embeddings usage factor — we do a lot of embeddings for search — is that priced the same way?
06:38 Lena: Embeddings are separate units, we can include them in the commitment band or set a different band for embeddings. Typically customers pick a hybrid: huge commit on inference tokens and a smaller embeddings commit.

09:02 Aisha: On the legal side, we need to know your baseline MSA and DPA. Any one-pagers or redlines we should expect?
09:10 Sam: Yes, we'll attach the standard MSA and DPA. Lena will share the DPA redline template we usually accept. We're generally flexible on a few clauses like data residency and audit rights.
09:26 Aisha: Audit rights are high priority. We have to ensure HelioPay can do annual audits and get access to logs for transactional data. Also want clarity on subcontractors and subprocessors.
09:36 Lena: For subprocessors we maintain a list; we do use cloud providers and some inference infra partners but we can provide a subprocessors list and add notification timing into the DPA. For audit access, we offer SOC 2 Type II and can provide audit artifacts on redacted basis.

12:10 Tara: On encryption, we run an internal policy that requires customer-managed keys for production PII. Do you support BYOK / KMS integration?
12:19 Lena: Yes, customer-managed KMS is supported for Private deployments (VPC or on-prem). For Hosted API we support envelope encryption with customer KMS in some regions — we should validate region-by-region.
12:34 Tara: If we go hosted, we need confirmation that keys are never persisted by Redwood. Also log retention and access control for decrypted payloads.
12:45 Lena: Understood. We'll include a short KMS architecture note in the docs we send. For hosted, keys are used for envelope encryption and not held in plaintext within our systems; detailed cryptographic flow will be included.

15:00 Ravi: On billing cadence — we prefer monthly true-ups but some of our execs push for quarterly invoicing to reduce card fees. Can you do quarterly invoices with monthly reporting?
15:12 Diego: Yes, we can support quarterly invoicing for committed usage and provide monthly usage reports for reconciliation. That will be in the SOW.

18:20 Marcus: Procurement wants an expected timeline from signature to provisioning — especially for dedicated pools — so we can plan migration windows. What's realistic?
18:30 Lena: Dedicated pool provisioning is typically 2-4 weeks after signature depending on region and capacity, sometimes faster if there's pre-approval for hardware. Hosted access is immediate after onboarding.
18:43 Marcus: 2-4 weeks is reasonable. Any prerequisites?
18:47 Diego: We'll need technical contacts, network connection info for private, and for dedicated we require a capacity creation request form which we'll share.

21:05 Aisha: For the MSA redlines — what clauses are typically firm from Redwood's side? Limitation of liability, indemnity, data retention?
21:14 Sam: Limitation of liability and IP carve-outs are fairly standard. We can be flexible on DPA operational bits but MSA's liability caps are often tied to the level of commitment.
21:28 Aisha: We'll need to escalate if our legal asks for a lower liability cap. Also please confirm your export controls / OFAC compliance language.
21:36 Lena: We'll include the standard compliance appendix. If HelioPay has particular export-control workflow requirements, let us know and we'll flag for our legal ops.

24:50 Tara: Quick question re: audit logs — what granularity do you retain and what is the retention window? We need transaction-level logs for 12 months.
24:58 Lena: We retain request/response logs for 90 days by default; extended retention to 12 months is available as an add-on (and often part of enterprise packages). We can also provide hashed payloads if needed for privacy.
25:14 Tara: Ok that add-on will be necessary. What's the cost profile?
25:20 Sam: It's usage plus storage; we'll show numbers in the spreadsheet.

28:00 Marcus: One procurement procedural item: do you require a PO before signature or do you accept signature+SOW and then a PO?
28:07 Diego: Both patterns are supported. Many customers sign MSA+SOW and then issue PO for the first invoice. If HelioPay requires PO pre-signature, we can accommodate but need to confirm billing contacts.

30:40 Ravi: If we sign annual commit do you offer seat-like discounts on platform fees or is it strictly per-token/embedding?
30:48 Sam: There are platform fees for some features (longer retention, extra observability retention) — we can discount platform fees as part of an enterprise package. For tokens/embeddings you get volume discounts as commit increases.

33:55 Aisha: Regarding DPA redlines — we will send our team's preferred language around data deletion and cross-border transfers. Are you willing to add an audit clause that allows our third-party auditor access?
34:05 Lena: We can include a scoped auditor access clause; usually it's limited to specific artifacts and under NDA. We'll share precedent language.

36:30 Marcus: Who will be the commercial point of contact for invoicing? We need a single billing owner on Redwood side.
36:36 Diego: Diego will be the billing owner for onboarding, Sam will own commercial terms during negotiation. We'll include billing contact details in the SOW.

39:00 Ravi: To the question about embeddings-heavy workloads: can you structure a mixed plan where embeddings overage is cheaper because it's smaller compute?
39:08 Lena: Yes, technically embeddings have a different compute profile; we can offer a dedicated embeddings pool or a specialized pricing line. We'll model both in the pricing spreadsheet.

42:12 Tara: On SSO, we need SAML + SCIM provisioning for teams. Do you support automatic user provisioning and role-based access?
42:21 Sam: Yes, SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning are supported. Role-based RBAC with granular perms is available in the Console. We'll include documentation links.

45:00 Aisha: Timeline we want: legal to do initial read and redlines within a week, procurement wants pricing approved within 5 business days afterwards. Is that workable?
45:12 Sam: That is doable if we turn around the pricing spreadsheet today and Lena sends SOC2/DPA baseline. Then Aisha's team can send redlines by next Wednesday and we can align internal approvals.

48:30 Marcus: Any unusual exclusions in the MSA that procurement should know about? For example, termination for convenience notice windows?
48:39 Sam: Standard termination windows are 30-90 days depending on commitment length. For annual committed contracts it's typically 60 days. We'll show exact language.

51:00 Tara: For KMS, what providers do you support? AWS KMS, GCP CMEK, Azure Key Vault — all three?
51:07 Lena: We support AWS KMS and GCP CMEK today. Azure Key Vault support is in progress; if HelioPay is Azure-first we can fast-track or propose a private deployment.
51:20 Tara: We are multi-cloud but primary on Azure; will need that clarified.
51:25 Lena: Noted — we'll include the Azure workarounds and expected timeline.

54:30 Diego: Recap of next steps — I'll summarize so nothing's missed: Sam will send pricing spreadsheet; Lena will attach SOC2 + KMS note + DPA baseline; Aisha will send HelioPay's DPA redlines; Ravi will confirm commit band; schedule a technical preflight with Tara.
54:47 Marcus: Sounds good, we'll aim for internal alignment this week.
54:54 Sam: Great, thanks all. We'll follow up with the docs and target the two-week goal to finalize commercial terms.
55:05 Aisha: Thanks everyone.
55:06 Ravi: Thanks.
55:08 Lena: Thanks, talk soon.
55:12 Diego: Bye.
---
Notes: occasional transcription artifacts present; speaker overlap in first minute. References to pricing figures omitted intentionally — will be provided in spreadsheet.
